$schema_note: Maps release artifacts to their Nexus Mods targets. To publish, create a GitHub Release tagged '<artifact>-v<version>' (e.g. nczoningcore-v1.0.0). The release.yml workflow parses the tag, stages contentDir into installDir, zips it as '<fileBaseName>_v<version>.zip' (so 'r6/...' sits at the zip root), attaches the zip to the release, and uploads to Nexus via Nexus-Mods/upload-action (beta.8, v3 upload API). See RELEASING.md.
$paths_note: contentDir = repo folder whose CONTENTS ship. installDir = path inside the zip those contents are placed at (the in-game install path under the Cyberpunk 2077 root). fileBaseName = the download filename stem (version is appended). NCZoningCore is pure redscript - loose .reds files, no WolvenKit packing.
$contentdir_note: contentDir is 'r6' and NOT 'r6/scripts/NCZoningCore', because the mod ships TWO trees: the scripts, and r6/storages/RedscriptConfigFramework/NCZoningCore.docs.txt, which is the in-game documentation page RCF renders in its hub (DVRCF_Docs reads <modId>.docs.txt from its own storage folder). Narrowing this back to the scripts folder silently drops the docs page from the download while every test that reads the REPO still passes. Before writing 'the download includes X' anywhere, check this key rather than the repo.
$file_id_note: The Nexus file id is NOT stored here. It lives in a REPOSITORY VARIABLE named NEXUS_FILE_ID_<ARTIFACT> (uppercased, '-' -> '_'), set under Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions > Variables. Two reasons: (1) a file_id DOES NOT EXIST until the mod's first file has been uploaded to Nexus BY HAND, so committing a placeholder commits a lie; (2) it is deployment config, not source. It is a VARIABLE and not a secret because it is an identifier, not a credential -- it authorizes nothing without NEXUSMODS_API_KEY, and masking it would only make a wrong id harder to debug. Get it from the mod page's Files tab > 'API Info' (Nexus labels it 'Group ID'). DO NOT use the file_id from the public v1 API -- that is a different id space and the wrong value looks entirely plausible. The workflow still honours a `file_id` key here as a fallback, but new repos should not set one.
